  • incidence or geographical spread.[1]

questions.question: Give an account of Yersinia pestis infection, including its epidemiology, mode of transmission and prevention.
questions.solution_html:
• Give an account of Yersinia pestis infection, including its epidemiology, mode of
  • transmission and prevention. / [CO3]
  • - Yersinia pestis is a Gram-negative bacterium that causes plague. [1], found in rodents and
  • other small mammals. [1], - It spreads mainly through the bite of infected rat fleas
  • (Xenopsylla cheopis). [1]. - It also spreads through contact with infected animals and
  • respiratory droplets in pneumonic plague. [1]. - Symptoms include fever, chills and swollen
  • lymph nodes. [1]. - Prevention includes rodent and flea control, sanitation and early
  • antibiotic treatment. [1]

questions.question: Explain the amastigote and promastigote forms of Leishmania.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the amastigote and promastigote forms of Leishmania. / [CO4]
  • Amastigote: Round or oval-shaped, non-flagellated, found inside human macrophages.[3]
  • Promastigote: Elongated in shape; has a single anterior flagellum.- Found in the gut of
  • sandflies and transmitted to humans.[3]

questions.question: Explain how environmental factors influence the occurrence and transmission of disease.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how environmental factors influence the occurrence and transmission of disease.
  • / [CO2]
  • Climate change affects the survival of disease-causing organisms and vectors. Deforestation
  • increases contact between humans and wildlife. Water pollution spreads waterborne
  • diseases. Poor sanitation increases infectious disease transmission. Urbanisation and
  • overcrowding favour disease spread. Floods and droughts increase the risk of disease
  • outbreaks.[6]

questions.question: Explain the role of fruit bats in the transmission of Nipah virus.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the role of fruit bats in the transmission of Nipah virus. / [CO3]
  • Fruit bats are natural reservoirs of Nipah virus. They shed the virus through saliva and urine.
  • Contaminated fruits and date palm sap can transmit the virus. Humans may become
  • infected by consuming contaminated food. Infection can spread from animals such as pigs to
  • humans. Human-to-human transmission occurs through close contact with infected
  • persons.[6]
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
